name: pixd
desc: Visual binary data using a colour palette
why: Renders arbitrary binary data as colour-palette pixels, a striking visual transform that reveals structure in any file.

brief.what_it_is: pixd is a command-line tool for visualizing binary data using a colour palette. It takes a binary file and prints each octet as a coloured square, so the output reads like a hexdump but with colour blocks in place of hex digits. The README gives no detailed input or output description beyond that.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames pixd as a visual counterpart to a hexdump tool: a different way to look at the same bytes. It gives no further motivation.
brief.how_it_works: pixd renders each octet as a coloured square using 24-bit colour SGR escape sequences in the terminal. The README says the code is based on the author's hexd tool, a more conventional colourful hexdump.
brief.standout: Each byte becomes one coloured square, so structure in a file shows up as visual patterns rather than hex digits. It is a colour-block take on the hexdump idea, and it borrows its code from the author's hexd project.
brief.status: unknown. The README has no release date, version, or changelog, and the fetched page showed no commit information.
brief.caveats: Output depends on a terminal with 24-bit colour SGR support, and the README links to a community gist for a list of compatible emulators. The README has no usage section, no example commands, and no install instructions. The scout notes describe pixd as revealing structure in any file, but the README does not make that claim; it only compares the tool to a hexdump. The screenshot is referenced by a relative path (meta/examples.png) that I did not fetch.
quotes: pixd is a tool for visualizing binary data using a colour palette.
in a lot of ways akin to a hexdump tool, except using coloured squares to represent each octet.
